summary: Choose self-referential programs by one computable parameter map, and transport the construction through explicit translations between program numberings.
abstract: Given a parameter, can one algorithm produce a program whose behavior uses that very program’s index? The ordinary recursion theorem promises an appropriate program for each separate request; a uniform construction gives a single primitive-recursive procedure selecting an index from the parameter. Equality here includes divergence as well as returned values. The same self-reference works in any acceptable numbering, meaning one with computable translations to and from the standard program list that preserve behavior. Jointly computable evaluation and coverage of all partial recursive functions alone are insufficient: an explicit listing makes halting at zero visible in its names and thereby prevents an effective compiler in the reverse direction.
